brief: CFTC data through September 29 show Non-Dealer S&P 500 futures selling continuing: Non-Dealers sold $10.5bn September 22-29, a 5th week of selling in six since August 18 for a net -$63.7bn, with long unwinds over 70% of the move since August 18. Categorically, Asset Manager led, selling $11.7bn ($5.5bn of it net liquidation); Other sold $1.1bn; Hedge Fund and Non-Reportable bought $620mm and $1.6bn. The Asset Manager liquidation coincided with a 25bp jump in 10-year real yields, pushing the Asset Manager gross-longs/real-yields correlation deeply negative, and quarter-end proximity suggests reallocation began early. Subsequently, below-consensus PCE, dovish Fed speakers and a weak Nonfarm payrolls print cut October hike pricing, lifting the S&P 0.70%. But the December Adjusted Interest Rate future, a funding proxy, cheapened ~5bps, so futures flows arguably stayed bearish despite the bounce. With Asset Manager net length still at a 77% 2-year rank as of Sept 29 (before incorporating further probable sales), GS expects ongoing pressure until yields reverse; GS's own rates research sees a skew toward lower yields, though oil and AI-investment resilience could push the other way.
